title.value: Investigating Mixture Policies in Entropy-Regularized Actor-Critic

TLDR.value: We study the benefit of mixture policies in entropy-regularized reinforcement learning with continuous action spaces

abstract.value: We study mixture policies in entropy-regularized reinforcement learning. Mixture policies offer greater flexibility than base policies like Gaussians, which we show theoretically provides improved solution quality and robustness to the entropy scale. Despite these potential benefits, they are rarely used for algorithms like Soft Actor-Critic, potentially due to the fact that Gaussians are easily reparameterized to get lower variance gradient updates, but mixtures are not. We fill this gap, introducing reparameterization gradient estimators for the mixture policy. Through extensive experiments on environments from classic control, MuJoCo, the DeepMind Control Suite and a suite of randomly generated bandits, our results show that mixture policies explore more efficiently in tasks with unshaped rewards (across entropy scales), while performing comparably to base policies in tasks with shaped rewards, and are more robust to multimodal critic surfaces.
